tips.comment: After the non-runners, I'm turning towards the Fergal O'Brien yard again, with his unbeaten novice Horaces Pearl. He was mightily impressive when winning at Newbury's big February meeting on going much softer than ideal.

Has 3 wins and 3 placed runs from 8 career starts. Wins coming on good and good to soft goings and has been placed in Grade 1 and Grade 2 races. Could make the frame again with race cut up with 3 non-runners including Lulamba.

Honesty Policy is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Gordon Elliott and is a progressive winner of the last two races. Up in class but open to improvement at a new trip, given dam Molo performed best around this trip and is a third foal related to two winners, notably Cuthbert Dibble, who posted a career-high RPR of 142 over 3m, so stamina shouldn't be an issue. On penultimate start, slammed Come Walk With Me by 8l, a horse who has since been beaten 1.75l by the Willie Mullins-trained Redemption Day, who is rated 140. Big chance under Mark Walsh.

Connections paid a huge 660k for him after he won his bumper. Stable in form and connections won the opening race yesterday. Has some decent form in the book, on hurdles debut beating one almost 10 lengths who was placed in GP1s the next twice. Ground will suit him more than most.

Won a hurdle race last time out, staying on strongly but being heavily eased at the finish of 2m 4f on yielding ground under today's jockey. Only a 5-year-old, so improvement to come as he steps up in grade. Sneaks into each-way bet @11/2.

Kappa Jy Pyke won a 21-runner maiden by 17 lengths at Punchestown when his only challenger fell at the last. However, he faded at the Cheltenham Festival behind The New Lion when trying this kind of distance for the first time. This is easier with defections.
He is a constant one, finishing in the top 3 in each of the last 4 races, and soon I expect a victory for him. This is looking like a pretty open race, so Good And Clever might produce an upset.

CASTLE CARROCK does give the impression he is a big price having caught the eye in Grade 2 novice hurdle company latest. He represents a powerful shrewd British dual-purpose yard and so in a race where an each-way play could be the way to go he appeals.

I fancied this horse in the Supreme at the Cheltenham Festival to run a big race, and although he eventually finished 9th and was well beaten, given another chance here, he should be involved on better ground and a longer straight, stepping up in distance.

Imperial Saint is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Philip Hobbs and Johnson White. He has a perfect profile for this contest with 5 out of 11 wins and 3 out of 6 as a chaser. He is twice a winner on today's good ground, and all his three chase wins have come at Aintree on today's Mildmay course, so we have a course specialist on our hands. He steps up in trip to 25f, and this could prove to be a smart move, being a winner of a 24f PTP. The excellent Michael Nolan rides, and Imperial Saint is my short-priced banker of the day.

Not a solid proposition by any means. He's now 11 years old also and missed 2 years of racing due to injury. So it remains to be seen how much ability he has left intact. Since joining this stable, he's run in 2 ultra-competitive handicaps at Cheltenham. He ran okay after a long break on reappearance and stable debut back in January, finishing in 5th place off a 4 lbs higher mark than this. He ran like he desperately needed that run. He ran a belter in the Ultima last time out. Made stealthy progress, running on into 4th place, beaten 15 lengths by the winner. The winner did win that race by 11 lengths, so it's not as bad a run as it sounds. He's been dropped another 1 lb for that effort. He won this race back in 2021 off a 10 lbs higher mark. I think he can run into a place at least if repeating the last effort.

Docpickedme comes here fresh following a break of 70 days since winning at Doncaster and he previously just lost out to bottom weight Charlie Uberalles also at Doncaster. Charlie Maggs rode him last time and his allowance takes his weight down to ten stone and Aintree suits frontrunners like Docpickedme.

Trainer Dan Skelton won this race in 2023 with his 8yo Midnight River with a mark of 151. This time round he goes with Le Milos the 2022 Coral Gold Cup Chase winner off a mark of 146 and gets in here off 142. Admittedly he is not as consistent as he used to be but is still capable of running a big race.
This one has got 6 lbs less to carry, and they have got the same regular jockey on board. A good value each way bet for the 4 places available.

Has given his new yard 3 solid efforts. A win at Doncaster, 5th and LTO was a very good 4th at Cheltenham in the Kim Muir. Was going well there until a mistake probably cost him. Might not be far away and, barring any mistakes, could be winning.

Cruz Control won this race last year and is only 3 pounds higher. Horses by his sire Saint Des Saints have been running well at Aintree this week, and it could be worth backing Imperial Saint also, who is by the same sire.
Interesting profile, and it suits the previous winners of this race. Strong stayer late. If this race falls apart, this will definitely pick up the pieces. Nice each-way value.

This race is cutting up badly with many runners out of form or up in class with plenty to improve. Erne River comes into this race off a good performance at Doncaster. The key to this horse is his jumping and keeping him interested in the race. Will be staying on late and fast. Each way only.

The experienced Sam Brown has an excellent statistical record here at Aintree. Despite his age, he is in good form as evidenced by his win at Newbury on 1 March. The chances of a podium finish look very strong. Chad Bament claims 7 lb.

Shakem Uparry hasn't had the best of seasons, but if Pauling has him right here, it could be another big win for Harry Redknapp. This has obviously been the main target and looks ready in the weights.

Was running well until 4 out at Cheltenham last time out. Different, and more suitable race conditions today. Yard form a little worry but is a capable and consistent performer at this kind of trip and grade.

Kitzbuhel is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Willie Mullins and ridden by Paul Townend. He is 2/2 wins since joining the Mullins yard and looks very talented. He is already rated 153, handles today's trip and good ground, and is owned by Mrs. J Donnelly, who has 96 winners from 305 runners in the UK and Ireland in the last five years. She is an owner who has tasted plenty of success at Aintree with horses such as Salvator Mundi and Dancing City. Big chance.
If TEAHUPOO has recovered from his hard race in the Stayers at Cheltenham, he should prove hard to beat. Travels within himself in the race, and ground and track are no issue.

I fancy Olly Murphy's staying hurdler to repeat last year's win at a course he loves and on ground that suits. He's had a wind-op following Ascot's Long Walk debacle in December and underwhelmed in the Cleeve Hurdle on Cheltenham's Trials Day. But Prestbury has never been his track, and back to the venue of his greatest success, he looks the one to be on.

Was on a hat trick last time out after wins in a Grade 2 and Grade 1 in Ireland but was unlucky on that hat trick bid when being hampered and unseating the rider in the Paddy Power Stayers at Cheltenham. It's 100/30 the field at the moment, so a bit open. So, fair each way bet @13/2.
I've followed Gwenie May Boy throughout, and I'll stick with it again. It just keeps improving, and yes, it's getting tough, but the Skelton team likes this race.

The Wallpark was a big fancy for many top tipsters at the Festival, but despite that confidence, it only managed to place. To me, that was still a good race as the pace didn't suit this horse, and it got outpaced before staying on at the finish.

There are plenty of cases, and whilst 8 females have attempted to win this getting 7lbs and not win this, I did find the case for Jetara an interesting one given the last 4 mares to run in this race have filled 4 places on 5 occasions (Roksana 2nd twice). She was a gutsy winner of a Grade 2 when keeping Kateira at bay late on over 3m. Dropped in trip since, she did well to stick on for 4th in the Mares Hurdle in a race that’s been soundly franked since. She’ll need a career-best to win here, but she’ll cope with the ground, and De Boinville has ridden her too, so he’s an interesting booking. He was on when he took her to a Grade 1 2nd behind Ballyburn about a year ago, which is form that also entitles her to respect when staying on well despite a mistake at the last.

With the ground described as good already, I expect these conditions to get even quicker during the day, so I suspect several of the main fancied horses will have it all to do. I’m going for a long shot in Altobelli, who has something to find on official terms but has been improving markedly since stepping up in distance with the new headgear. Always highly regarded and given plenty of time to mature, the now 7-year-old was clearly running over inadequate trips on too testing ground and bolted up in competitive handicaps at Ascot the last twice, giving the impression he could actually go another lap of the track. The yard won this race in 2019 with If The Cap Fits, who was also stepping up in distance for the first time, so at around 22/1 he could outrun his odds and have a chance for a place in the frame.

Hiddenvalley is still very lightly raced for an 8 year old and is still open to improvement. He goes very well fresh and his last run can be forgotten as the trainer was in very poor form at the time. He can outrun his odds in this race.
This horse has a very good record here at Aintree. Had a few lbs to find on ratings with a few of these, but on this track and with decent ground to suit, he can outrun his odds.

Teahupoo is the standout horse if playing to his strengths. I'm not sure about the Elliott yard at the moment though, so at odds, we can take a small chance with Buddy One. The selection reserves his best form for decent ground - he'll get that today - and can go close barring accidents.

Winner of a Listed hurdle at Perth over three miles in April last year, Sounds Russian makes some each-way appeal at a big price for trainer Ruth Jefferson. Five wins from 16 career starts. Quality efforts over fences and didn't run too badly on sole previous outing to Aintree. Hasn't had that much racing really for a ten-year-old. Has shown a lot of promise. Numerous placed efforts in Graded company.

I Am Maximus is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Willie Mullins. He bolted up by 7.5 lengths in last year's Grand National and is just 8 pounds higher. He beat some classy horses like Delta Work, who had won six graded races, and Minella Indo, who had won seven graded races. That was an impressive performance which can be repeated given a clear round under Paul Townend.

Iroko has been losing unpurpose in every race this season, which would probably make him the best handicapped horse here. The fast ground should help any stamina doubts, which leaves the question if he's capable of jumping these type of fences. McManus probably decided not to run the Gold Cup winner, as he's confident enough with the horses he has here. It's just the question which one will win.

Stumptown, an 8-year-old, has proved his ability with four consecutive wins over trips up to 3m5f, including the Cross Country at Cheltenham last time, when looking as if he would stay all day. He was traveling well over 4m1f at Punchestown five runs ago, with 5 to jump when a loose horse took him out. Accurate jumper and Keith's in the saddle.

Strong runner in Ireland, emphasized by two good wins at Leopardstown in fields of twenty-five and twenty-seven runners. Unknown whether the Irish raider will take to Aintree as easily, with whole career across the sea. Good each-way value nevertheless.
The trainer has got no less than 6 entered in this race, and they have got an interesting jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet for the 6 places available.

The Shark Hanlon Irish-trained Hewick cost only an unbelievable €800. He may be small in stature, but he jumps for fun and has a big heart. The King George VI Chase winner will love the ground, and he is reunited with Gavin Sheehan for the first time since their 2023 King George VI win. He ticks most of the right boxes: aged 10 ??', handicap mark of 157 ??', 6 out of last 8 Irish-trained ??', won lto ??', won over fences ??'. He is unproven over the 35f trip but has won tw0 Chases over 29f. I think this is a very good renewal, but one thing they all need is a bit of luck.

Stole the show back at last year's Irish National, taking a Fairyhouse hatrick. The ground here today is completely different, but I was impressed enough with Raffles that he stuck in my mind. He has it in him to at least place.

Vanillier finished 2nd behind Corach Rambler in the 2023 Grand National and ran last in the Cross Country Race at the Cheltenham Festival. A jockey error at the fence, which mimics the Canal Turn, saw him lose around 20 lengths by carrying straight on and almost crashing through the outer rails. However, he recovered to finish 3rd and should go well from near the bottom of the handicap.

I've always thought the 'Hennessy' was a good trial for the National, and this lad won it quite easily this season. Still unexposed, Nicholls' horses seem to be running well at the moment, and Cobden is riding superbly. At the moment, everything seems in place for a big run.

I've waxed lyrical to anybody that would listen for the past few months that should Gordan Elliott's 8 year old Gelding THREE CARD BRAG get into this race he could potentially be very dangerous. This lad didn't run awfully In the paddy power over Christmas @Leopardstown running on ground he wouldn't have been in love with yet still had some juggernauts in behind him. He has a ¾ length second behind CORBETT'S CROSS & 2nd place behind MONTYS STAR on his résumé. He looks a stayer (wether he can take on this marathon trek is another question) & is fairly unexposed on this type of going ( I would have preferred a bit of juice in the ground I won't lie) but being a Son of JETAWAY he has the pedigree for the ground. The booking of Jockey Sean Bowen is very promising who arrives here in fine fettle with 16 wins this past month. Ive got to live by the sword here & back this feather light lad.

This selection's best effort to date was a 3rd place finish over the distance of 34.5 furlongs. Racing over 34.5 furlongs in today's contest, hopeful the ground will suit. Rachael Blackmore is retained and has each-way appeal.
This horse has looked very progressive this season. Should love the underfoot conditions and is open to improvement after just a handful of chases.

7th last year, only faded on the run-in. That was an amazing effort for a 7-year-old and should improve as an 8-year-old now. 1 lb lower in weight this year, Danny Mullins picks him over Minella Cromer. A decent fun bet at 25s.

It's been a very long time since Twiston Davies won the Grand National, but as a trainer, he has won it two times. The last one was in 2002. He is due another one, and this horse is going a bit under the radar. It looks progressive and comes out well on trends.

Won both of the last two, including a Grade Three at Fairyhouse over three and a quarter miles last time out. Had the re-opposing Intense Raffles and Minella Cocooner behind that day and looks a massive price for each way purposes, with many bookies paying out on extra places.

I've convinced myself That Gordan Elliott's 8 year old Gelding DUFFLE COAT has a big run in him, This Son of ALHEBAYEB goes off here at huge 66/1 odds & I can't for the life of me understand why. This charge was throwing down a challenge last month @Cheltenham (30f Good/Soft) & looked to be atleast hitting the crossbar (in my humble opinion) before being brought down 2 out, This however isn't a flash In the pan, this charge put in some big game performances (again at big odds) finishing ½ a length in 2nd in the Galway Plate. All in all this charge has a 61.54% place strike rate over the tall timber with ground conditions looking to suit. Jockey Danny Gilligan remains in the pilot seat & has a 50% place strike rate whilst in the plate. Prior to last time outs run @Cheltenham I would have questioned this lads stamina but at these odds with 6 places on offer I'll let this Grey lad carry my Each way Pennies.

Solid performer who has only been seen a couple of times this season but has run well on both occasions and only beaten a nose off this mark at Ascot last time. Some stamina questions but was 4th in the 2023 Scottish National so every chance he could outrun his odds.

SENIOR CHIEF is a horse I can see having a say in the finish in this year's Grand National. Hailing from the very shrewd De Bromhead yard, the prep looks like it's been geared for this race since disappointing in the Irish Grand National. The selection was pulled up in that race off a mark of 141, but he then won after a 208-day absence at Cheltenham in October, off a mark of 142 in first-time cheekpieces, which bumped his handicap mark up enough to secure his spot in the Grand National. His jumping let him down at Newbury a month later, but connections have given him time to recover and gave him a spin over hurdles (without cheekpieces) over 2m7f to keep him ticking over and give his jumping a confidence boost. Cheekpieces are reapplied for the big one to help him concentrate on his jumping. He's still lightly raced enough to be improving past his handicap mark, and this stamina test looks within range off his nice weight.

33-1 is a big price for Grangeclare West despite the 11-08 he is allotted in this race. Second to Galopin Des Champs in the Grade 1 Irish Gold Cup at Leopardstown in February. Has only had six starts over fences (winner of two). Five wins from 11 starts under rules. Thorough staying pedigree by Presenting out of a Sir Harry Lewis mare. Should run a big race for in-form trainer Willie Mullins (SR 37%) and jockey Brian Hayes.

Well, I know the horse is out of fashion, but he makes a foray into handicap company for the first time in a long time. The distance is an issue, but on ground that is probably on the good side, he may find the distance and fences within his compass. A low mark for a horse of his quality. In James Reveley, he has a jockey who has blossomed in France since moving and is an intelligent rider. Providing it remains upright and makes no shuddering error, he has a chance to finish in the 6 places on offer at a price.
With 6 places, this horse could go very well. The horse has a great handicap mark. Gordon Elliot has a good record, and the drying ground is ideal for Fil Dor.

Twig ticks boxes for distances beyond 3 miles and for good ground. I recognize the ground is officially good to soft and the going stick has backed that up, but the evidence of my own eyes over the last 2 days at Aintree, added to the sunshine and breeze over the 3-day meeting, has left me focusing on the good ground horses. There are at least eight of them who have won on good ground. Last year was a new national - just an ordinary long-distance chase - so special jumping ability is no longer a requirement.

The fences could be the making of him. His mark is fine, having been placed off a pound lower in a decent handicap at Cheltenham last year. Been out of form the last twice, but this could be a decent outsider.

Monbeg Genius has drifted to a massive price considering his potential and ability. This is presumably down to jockey bookings, but the stable jockey is claimed by McManus for Iroko, and Nick Schofield always rides for these owners, so it is no surprise about the riding arrangements. He could surprise!
Strong stayer showed a hair more last time out in the Ultima without ever really being put into the race. Hard to know how he will take to the fences but they could be the making of him.
Useful Henderson horse who won many good races back in the day still retains that old ability. The GN fences are easy to jump now.

Absolutely in the dark about whether this 13-year-old will want this type of trip. BUT he has run over these fences 3 times in the past and, importantly, completed on each occasion. I just can't shirk that at the odds. However, caution is needed as he's on the highest mark of his career but comes into this race in good form. Today will be only his 30th race, so he is pretty lightly raced for a horse of this age and could run well.

Kalif Du Berlais is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Paul Nicholls. He is extremely progressive, winning 5 out of 8 races, and is seemingly a 2-mile specialist, having disappointed last time out over 2 miles 4 furlongs. He seems ground versatile, having been 1 length when falling at the last on good ground. His form of his penultimate start, beating Vincenzo by 9.5 lengths, looks solid with Vincenzo winning next time out, then finishing runner-up in a Grade 3 contest. Kalif Du Berlais can go close to adding another winner to Paul Nicholls' tally at Aintree.

Only By Night put in a monstrous run behind Jango Baie and Majborough at the Festival last time out and although Jango Baie disappointed the other day, this should be seen as decent enough form. Great chance here.

There was not much between L'eau Du Sud and Only By Night when they ran at the Cheltenham Festival. Harry Skelton hit the front earlier than he wanted when the favourite made a bad mistake at the second last. He was left in front and lost momentum jumping the last, dropping to 4th.

Touch Me Not has shown strong consistency this season, with two wins and a solid runner-up at Cheltenham. His 158 RPR confirms his jumping quality. Trained by Gordon Elliott and ridden by Sam Ewing, he arrives in form and ready to take on the top contenders in this Grade 1.

He's the 2nd lowest rated here, running off a mark of 142, but won his only spin over larger obstacles, winning a beginners chase at Thurles over 16f 58 days ago by 2.5L on good ground. He was an outsider that day with a 66/1 SP. Was with local trainer Pam Sly in the previous code, but trainer H. De Bromhead is very good with beginner/novice chasers at the minimum trip, and this one will relish the fast surface.

Le Labo is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien. He made a favorable impression winning on debut and is a fourth foal related to three individual winners, notably Presentandcounting, with 14/42 wins and an RPR of 150. The owner, Mrs. Claire Gleeson, owned A Dream To Share, who won the first three bumpers and was then sold to J.P. McManus and won the Cheltenham Festival bumper. So, the current owner has a good eye, and Le Labo could prove to be smart.

Mossy Fen Road is a really smart horse who won nicely at Wetherby. Trained by Harry Derham and ridden by Paul O'Brien. Harry reports that the key with Mossy is whether he settles, if he settles nicely then he’ll have a huge chance.

Willie Mullins's horses are outperforming at Aintree. Green Splendour is their entry for the Grade 2 bumper. Although only 5th in a Grade 2 bumper at Leopardstown last time, he could be good enough to go close here.

A well-supported favourite on racecourse debut at Naas in December, and although not everything went to plan, he stayed on strongly and ultimately looked impressive. 14/1 looks too big here and a worthy each-way chance.
Won his first bumper in Ireland and since ran fourth in his next two races at Leopardstown. He has ability with a decent pilot on board and could go close.
This one is 2 for 2. With the stable going well and the jockey riding plenty of winners, this one is the pick to improve enough to take what looks like a good race.
2 wins from 2 under rules. Finishes races strongly, showing good determination when pressed, has won on good ground at Warwick which has sharp bends like today.

Quaviste came there swinging on debut and picked up nicely, if looking very green late on. Considering he was switched off and had to round the field on the home bend, he found plenty even when wandering around late on, being strongest at the line. Up in trip here, he looks to me on that evidence like he can get competitive here. The horse he beat has won since and did come into that having had a run against one of the principals in here. Whilst that form also gives this horse a bit to find, I do think he can improve a jolt here. The yard's bumper horses have been faring well all season as an added bonus.

STORMING GEORGE runs for trainer Neil King who won this race in 2022. This second-up five year old has likely been set aside for this specific race and he has at least as sound a sire as any lining up. His debut win on similar ground can be improved upon and he could surprise.

There's obviously stacks of horses from bigger yards in this, but this French-bred 4yo beat a couple of well-fancied horses from bigger yards on his sole start. He gets the 4yo allowance here, which is particularly relevant since he's French-bred and therefore likely to have come to hand earlier. Only 8 of the 20 runner field are unbeaten, and the winner of this for the last 4 years has been unbeaten, so he ticks a few boxes for such a big outsider.
Huge odds on this one. Strong on speed figures, strong on ran-to-rating. Will be prominent, which is key in these races. This is massively overpriced in my opinion.
Won last time out, and that was improved form on the last two showings prior. Good trainer who does well at Aintree and good price.

Jennie Cavendish and Sean Quinlan are the form trainer and jockey duo at the moment and again team up on R&R to try and notch another winner. The horse has his ground and distance and should be somewhere close at the end.
Had a bit in hand when landed Handicap by 6L off 77 here last time. Trainer in form. Contender for hat-trick bid.

Time Was has been highly consistent, including a recent second at Newcastle. He fits this class well, and a drop in weight could be a key advantage. Carrying 11-0 and trained by the reliable Philip Kirby, there’s room for further progress and he looks capable of going close in this field.

Leader Wing can go well for the Boanas yard. Leader Wing was second over track and trip last time out and can do better with that race to work on. Leader Wing has won in a bumper before and can go well on today's ground.

She's A Rocca, a lightly raced 10-year-old, runs well at this track, unlike last time at Carlisle where she didn't like the undulations and was pulled up. Her penultimate start was here when keeping on for 2nd over 2m1f, good to soft. Her best win to date was in a class 4 at Southwell over 2m4f, good, in October 2023 off a 4lb higher mark. She has 2m4f and good ground today along with the rider's claim. The price offers some very good value at 16/1.
Is yet to trouble the judge in four novice hurdles but strikes as the sort who could make significant progress now moving into handicaps from a modest mark. Worth considering.

Top weight 'Genois' isn't out of this at big odds back on better ground. But I feel my selection looks to have a lot in his favor today and has a huge chance on his 2nd of 7 to 'Tedley' at Wetherby (2m 3f 85yds) on good ground in a Class 3 Handicap Chase back in November last year when only beaten 1 and a 1/4 lengths. He must surely be hard to beat on that run of only a 2lb higher mark.

I'm keen to oppose the overnight favourite here who last time out ran over more than 4 miles and is entitled to be feeling some effects. Frequently tapped for toe and finishing second over shorter trips is also held against him. Cerendipity, who may challenge Choosethenews for favouritism, is a winner last time out and only one pound up in the handicap. With a sire that preferred soft ground there may be a question over today's good ground, but he has been okay on good to soft, so Cerendipity is the choice.

Race 4 at Newcastle is the Val And Kath Bollado Memorial Handicap Chase (Class 3) for 5-year-olds and upwards over 4,040 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 9-year-old gelding Immortal Fame from the Deborah Cole yard and will be ridden by Jordan Nailor. This son of Fame and Glory is in scintillating form, winning three of his last 5 and finishing 2nd and 3rd in the remaining two. With an overall haul of 8 wins from 24 starts and a host of runner-up finishes, he just has to be included in all calculations.
Four runs this campaign for the 8yo, getting his act together three weeks ago when beaten under a length at this track. Every chance off his current mark and no problem with the quicker ground.

At 11 years old, he is probably a bit high in the weights to win after winning a couple of races at the back end of last year. But he is well in on old form, and conditions will suit. Returns after a break and has performed well in the past after a break. EW bet.
Followed up last time and comes here unpenalized. In fact, he is 3lb better off because his jockey in that last win is able to claim his 3lb, unlike in that last win. Has to be backed here.

This one is inconsistent, and his last win came in November 2023. But he takes up the chase every so often. Having dropped 1 grade and 1 lb after the latest run, he is now 4 lb lower than the last win.
Top of the Bay, after a two hundred and seventy-five day break, ran a great race 2/7 last time out over course and distance. Well worth a win bet!

This one won 3 from 4 here last year, the latest of which was over C/D off 96. Not as good off higher marks since, including last time over various trips, but is now 3lb lower than his last win over C/D, a more suitable trip than 23.4f last time.

This N G Richards-trained 4-year-old gelding improved from his racecourse debut when second in a two-mile N H F race at Kelso to win his latest start in a two-mile one-furlong N H F race at Newcastle three weeks ago. He ran on strongly in the closing stages to beat the Miss Lucinda V Russell-trained Hunters Spring by two lengths. With Sean Quinlan onboard, he can defy his penalty and follow up today.

Real chancey one, but backing purely on the jockey record for the yard in bumper races where he has an 18% strike rate and 58% of his rides in this type finish in the first 3. Admittedly, the jockey has ridden this on both his runs in this sphere with no luck, but it is unlike the trainer to be wasting her time in races.
The Boola Boss turned in a nice performance last time when able to dominate. Has not been given too much more today and Jamie Brace has a 43% strike rate for this trainer (3 wins from 7)

This Ben Pauling runner is steadily getting the hang of chasing and opened his account at Southwell 24.3f on good ground last month. Does have a 5lb rise but is still finding his way chasing, and I think can go in again here this afternoon.
Consistent sort who's twice placed off similar marks, and returns fresh after a break and wind op. Ground suits and could capitalize if others underperform in this small field.
Now back on his last winning mark and showed promise last time; the ground may be quick enough, but he's dangerous if building on that recent effort. Not discounted.

Had regained some form on three of her recent starts finishing 2nd at Doncaster and 4th at both Newbury and at Chepstow. All of those starts came over three miles but failed to sparkle racing over a shorter trip at Warwick last time. Back up in trip at a more galloping track should see a stronger performance.

Have to forgive his poor showing last time. He has a tongue tie added for the first time today. He showed promise over an inadequate trip on the penultimate start, and on that basis, is worth a small punt.

Zambezi Fix has three wins to his name around here, and the 10-year-old has spent most of his racing in better class than today's. He has shown previously that he can act on good when 4th at Ascot in a class 2. Bumped into one last time, and the grey is given another chance today.

Bells Of Ufford has shown gradual improvement and now drops into a more manageable handicap class. Carrying top weight of 12-0 and partnered with Alan Johns, he could capitalise if repeating the promise shown at Hereford in February. The distance and ground conditions look ideal for him to step forward today.
Marco’s Light has yet to show much, but she’s unexposed, goes handicapping for the first time, and represents a shrewd yard. Big leap needed??'but not impossible in this low-grade contest.
Has been disappointing in both bumpers and 3 hurdles starts to date. Steps up in trip for handicap debut, and if finding some improvement, will have an each-way chance.

Rising Force looks primed to go close here. He comes into this on the back of two solid efforts in Class 5 company over a mile, and now drops into a weaker Class 6 contest. Last time out, he ran a blinder in a deep 21-runner field where the average rating was 64 ??' tomorrow’s race has an average rating of just 49, and the top-rated horse is 5lbs inferior to what he faced last time. Not only does he face weaker opposition, but he’s also set to carry 10lbs less than he did in that recent effort, while running off the same mark. On paper, this is a significant drop in class and pressure. If he reproduces anything close to his recent form, he’s got to be right there. Strong each-way claims. Good Luck!

Racing back on the turf this afternoon after running well on the all-weather as of late. Back up to the mile trip but is on a competitive mark, and with 5 places on offer, looks very good each-way value at these odds.

Race 1 at Yarmouth today is the QuinnBet Handicap (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,612 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 5-year-old mare Oh So Audacious from the Harry Eustace yard. She will be ridden by Kaiya Fraser. This daughter of Mukhadram is in some excellent form currently and is an obvious contender for top honors here, no doubt. Worth a go.

Anglo Saxon didn’t get much of a chance from a tough draw at Kempton last time, but he’s got a great record at Yarmouth with three wins here and loves to go forward. Decent jockey booked and back at a track that suits, he’s not out of it if he gets into a rhythm up front.

This one makes his handicap debut for the in-form stable of Michael Bell here off just 59, and that looks a potentially lenient mark to me. The horse has had the usual 3 quiet runs to get this mark, but there are clues that he's got some ability. The 2nd start, in particular, saw the horse steadied at the start, then switched, then just sitting out the back before making some ground late on to run into 5th of the 8 runners. The third has since won off a 24lb higher mark than JC races off here, and it might be that we see the horse's true ability now that he's sent handicapping.

A very open-looking low-grade handicap where Glastonbury makes a lot of appeal. A recent run will have him spot on, and he looks well handicapped at the moment. He won well here over the distance a few runs ago, and at 10/1 is nap material.

Course winner and has come close over this distance on a couple of occasions. He is on a mark where he can make an impact if it's one of his going days. There are some better horses in this race, which means his price will be worth a punt.

It has been 13 races since his last victory in 2024. Recently, at Southwell, he finished 7th out of 11 in a handicap race over 7.1 furlongs. However, with a skilled jockey in the saddle, if they can conserve the 7-year-old's energy for the final stretch, a place at 18/1 could yield a profitable return.

MOREGINPLEASE showed up on a few occasions at Yarmouth last season and also gets this distance so there's a chance returning to the turf from a rock bottom mark could see a change in fortune. Will definitely be happier in these surroundings and although risky for win purposes, there's a good each-way return on offer with the extra places.

A three-time winner (twice on turf) who likely needed the run when last of eight on his reappearance at Wolverhampton (6f) last month. However, he should strip fitter, and the turf will suit better as well as this further trip of a mile. He can race 8lb below his last winning mark, and the in-form Rob Hornby (3-13) takes his first ride on this animal.

Regal Agenda took a nice step forward from her debut when finishing second over 8f here and looked like she’d improve further. She’s up in trip now which should suit, and if she’s straight enough after the break, she’s definitely a threat in this.

Trainer R Beckett sends just the one runner over to Yarmouth, over a 200-mile trip, and has good stats for when the stable sends one runner long distance: 223/61 27% +71. This 3-year-old filly has had just one run, a promising third place at Ascot last September, where the form has been boosted.

One interesting Dubawi filly, sister of a Breeders' Cup winner (and the Breeders' Cup is one event I look forward to every year), and that the dam won the Ribblesdale in her career over 10 furlongs. This debut might be too long for a newcomer. However, good pedigree and should be on the shortlist. Cieren Fallon won only 5 times out of 40 odd winners for Godolphin, 3 wins out of 12 for trainer Appleby.

Not sure what he beat last time, and nothing has come out of the race with any type of subsequent performance. But he won impressively, comes from a good family, and cost 550k as a yearling, so he should be much better.

Palazzo Blu showed a great attitude to come from last to first and win narrowly on debut at Chelmsford, doing it with a bit in hand despite the tight margin. Back from a break now but looks a nice type with more to come, and definitely appeals as an improver to keep on side.

Probably performed better than expected in debut run on the flats in the U.K. when 4th of 8 at Wolverhampton in February of this year. If improvements are made, it has a chance tomorrow despite going up in class.

Always A Star was left flat-footed before staying on nicely for third at Newcastle, and the step up in trip looks like it’ll suit him well. The jockey booking catches the eye and with the yard doing well in turf handicaps, he looks set to go well if he keeps improving.
He was running well last term by the close of 2024 and should be able to go well after his layoff. Previous winner here and each-way material.

Kept on inside the final furlong and nearest at the finish over half a furlong shorter at Wolverhampton when last seen. Only tried this mile and a quarter trip once before at Goodwood last year where the heavy ground would not have suited and worth another look on the strength of that previous run.

Eljaytee was a reliable type at this level last summer, especially around here, and has won twice off this mark before. His form did tail off a bit late in the season, and he might just need this reappearance run, but he’s clearly capable if ready to go. Worth taking a chance on at big odds.
Makes seasonal reappearance for new trainer Boughey and is off the same mark as when runner-up on his last appearance in September. Been gelded and a strong showing is expected.

Dorney Lake didn’t quite get his head in front last season but was consistently not far off and has dropped from 90 to 81, which makes him look well treated now. He’s back from a break but the yard’s in form and the trainer-jockey combo does well in turf handicaps (28 runs, 6 wins, 21% strike rate, +5pts @ 18% ROI), so he’s definitely one to keep in mind if ready to go.

Won over this trip when sent off favorite at Newcastle on penultimate start but well beaten over this trip at Kempton when upped in grade to Class 3 seven days ago. Comes here race fit and should find this ease in grade to Class 4 a little easier.

At the bottom of the handicap mark in this field, and probably for good reason after the last time out effort when 8th of 8 at Wolverhampton. But has course experience and performed well last September. Has scored 2 wins over C&D, so should welcome a return back to this course.

Scarlet Lady hasn’t really been firing lately and her last run at Southwell was a bit flat, which lines up with her current form suggesting the mark might still be on the high side. That said, she did bolt up over C&D last August, and if she can bounce back to that kind of form, she’d take some stopping. Trainer-jockey combo does well in turf handicaps (10 runs, 4 wins, +%pts @ 50% ROI), so she’s not without hope.
Raised Mark has halted her progress after winning at Lingfield last July, but she has the ability to bounce back. This is helped by a dropped mark, and she is also a C&D winner.
Makes seasonal reappearance and handicap debut, and it looks like the money has come for him. Ridden with handicaps in mind last year and is expected to go well here.
Looked very impressive when winning last time out and is a much better horse than its rating suggests at the moment. I expect this one to continue to improve today with a follow-up win on the cards.

Calibos didn’t show much in his nursery run at Wolverhampton but had hinted at ability in novice races before that. He’s up in trip now and returns from a break, which could bring out some improvement. With the yard going well in turf handicaps (486 runs, 81 wins, 17% strike rate, +48pts @ 10% ROI), he’s worth a second look if there’s market support.

Squires Treaty hasn’t been at his best lately and was well held at Southwell last time, but he’s dropped to a mark that makes him look well treated if he can bounce back. The yard has a good record in turf handicaps (57 runs, 7 wins, 12% strike rate, +15pts @ 26% ROI), so if he can rediscover a bit of spark, he’s not without a chance.
Yet to win from 5 starts but did finish 2nd on penultimate outing. Remains open to improvement and holds an each-way chance.

Flast's career is not going to plan, and there was no change in fortune in the handicap debut LTO when only 7 of 8 at Southwell last month. However, it has course experience, so perhaps a return to this course might kickstart things, which is helped by a dropped mark and a drop down in class.

The use of cheekpieces for the first time had a positive impact last time out when a useful 4th of 11 at Wolverhampton. The hope is that she can carry that kind of form to turf and is helped by a dropped mark.

Pouting was well backed last time and ran to a fair level when beaten 2½ lengths in a Southwell nursery, which lines up with the rest of her form. She’s been consistent enough and that effort suggests she’s got a chance here if things fall right.
Bred to be useful but was clueless and green as grass on debut last September and was still very green on his second run the following month. Now with Beckett and expected to improve as a 3-year-old.

Race 1 at Wolverhampton today is the Best Odds Guaranteed At BetMGM Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Class 5) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,025 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old filly Peregrine Falcon from the Patrick Morris yard, and will be ridden by Joe Fanning. This daughter of Showcasing was thrust into a Gr3 at only her second start after a promising debut with a below-par performance there. Her next two were not bad, but she is down in class today, likely to get her confidence up. Worth a chance here, reading between the lines.

Has struggled for form this year, albeit only just 2 runs this year. But hoping down in trip helps her and makes course debut in a non-handicap race, which considering the high mark she has been running on, might just be a good thing.

Wine Dark Sea shaped really nicely on debut when second at Yarmouth, only beaten just over a length, and looked like one with plenty more to come. He’s up in trip and returns from a break, but that initial run was full of promise and he’s likely to step forward. Definitely one to take seriously.

Belgravian didn’t show much on debut at Bath, looking green and slowly away, but he’s up in trip now and comes from a yard that knows how to bring them on. He’ll need to step up quite a bit, but there should be plenty of improvement to come with that experience under his belt.

Second run here after wind operation where in his first run back he actually looked more positive than the result may suggest. Came 4/7 over 6f, but ran well into the finish and was gaining on the leaders. Another furlong and he would've come very close. He runs over 7f today and has a half-decent draw. Good market support.

Tricky handicap, this one, with 4 horses standing out to me. This one got the vote through its 2 useful-looking C/D outings as of late. 3rd last time out here and goes off the same mark this afternoon.

Risk ran a decent race last time when beaten just under a length at Lingfield in first-time visor, which he keeps on here. He’s gone well over C&D before and while he’ll need a bit more to win this, he’s not without a chance if things drop right.

Race 3 at Wolverhampton today is the Weekly Free Bets With BetMGM Extra Handicap (Div 1) (Class 5) for 3-year-olds over 1,441 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old gelding Packetofbiscuits from the Sir Mark Prescott yard, and will be ridden by Rhys Clutterbuck. This son of Showcasing is extremely unfortunate not to have a victory, with his last two being beaten by a neck. He rates as a top contender here and has to be included.

Blue Seeker is unlikely to be a leading-light in the Crisford yard, but he should be capable of picking up a class 5 handicap. He won a class 6 nursery over 7 furlongs in December and for some reason was stepped up to 8.5f last time out against the well-handicapped Tuco Salamanca. Blue Seeker's pedigree suggested he might not stay. He is on a fair mark and the jockey can claim a valuable 5 pounds.
This horse has new headgear fitted for today and may show some improvement off what looks to be a very fair handicap mark.

STANDPUT was progressing well on the Tapeta with a CD win here in January, and a competitive follow-up at Southwell. If you are prepared to forgive the run on the Polytrack at Kempton last time out, which looked on the slow side, there could be a big run at a tasty price here. Not drawn out of it either.

Not seen since July, where he was a backward 2-year-old, rough around the edges and still learning. This means he comes here from a competitive mark, as he is certainly capable of much more than he showed last year.

Florida Dawn didn’t fire last time at Newcastle, finishing a well-beaten third, but conditions should suit better here and he looks well treated now going into handicaps. If he bounces back to anything like his earlier promise, he’s a big threat in this lineup.
Finished runner-up in both its handicap outings as of late, including one over C/D. Looks like the best form on offer in this race, and with 4 places up for grabs, should be amongst them.

Shown more than enough in his runs for a mark to think that he is capable of picking up a race. An opening mark of 69 is not the most generous but he has a smart 5lb claimer helping his burden and that can be enough.

Arabian Cobra’s been pretty consistent and wasn’t beaten far last time over 6f at Southwell after racing a bit freely. Back up to 7f now, which suits based on his only try at the trip, and he’s usually there or thereabouts.
Both previous runs have been at Newcastle over 6f, where it improved on a 3rd place debut performance with a win last time. Steps up in trip and holds every chance if finding more improvement.

Optimatum hasn’t shown a ton yet but did travel alright for a bit at Newcastle before fading out of it. He’s back from a break now and has stuck to 7f so far, so could have more to offer with a bit of time and a switch to handicaps.
3rd over course and distance before his 162-day break. Drops 1lb for his return, and Mark Loughnane does well with 3-year-olds at this track. So, no surprise to see the horse go well after a break.
Another newly gelded on the all-weather, and this 3-y-o is in good form, winning the last two and could be tough to stop the hat-trick bid. Makes handicap debut and can have more to come.

I think this race will be set up for him with at least two trying to make all, so likely to be a decent pace on which leaves it open for a finisher. He has already beaten Desert Champion off levels in February and now receives 8 lb off him on handicap debut.

Won over C&D off 71 back in September, most recent outing looked like a much needed run after a 163 day break post yard move. Off 77 today, others are giving him a lot of weight and I think if he breaks well, he is definitely in with a chance.
FOREVER PROUD should be there or thereabouts here. The stable are back in form and do well here at Wolverhampton, and there's clearly a feeling that he should be winning again before too long.
A very open-looking seller's race. Boatsy is down in grade and has dropped down the weights. Maybe it is his time for a resurgence today in this race. EW bet.

Genuine mare won over this course and distance in February and made it back-to-back wins last month to take her career total to 8 victories. Decent efforts here the last twice, and it is a little surprising to see her dropped to this grade.

Danehill Star showed a bit of grit to win at Lingfield in January and wasn’t disgraced in a classified race last time. The visor goes on for the first time which could sharpen him up, and he’s back in a winnable sort of race. Worth a look if the headgear gives him a boost.
Kept on inside the final furlong over a mile and a quarter at Newcastle last time out and of interest taking this slight drop in trip.

Orchid looked right at home over this trip when winning easily at Kempton last time and now tries Tapeta for the first time. Tongue-tie goes on and the trainer’s in good form, plus the trainer-jockey combo has been profitable (157 runs, 27 wins, 17% strike rate, +6pts @ 4% ROI). If she handles the surface, she’s got strong claims of following up.
Well on top finish when winning last time, and the 6lb extra should be manageable to allow her to follow up in this race.

Certainly thriving as of late, consistently running well. Won over the 6 furlongs last time out and goes well at this course as well. Has gone up in the ratings as expected but should make the frame at least.

Where's Clare did too much early when last seen at Ayr in September but has shown she goes well at sharp tracks like this, and the trip suits her. She might need this after the break, but the yard’s in good form, and she’s not one to completely rule out if she’s tuned up.
She ran well lately over 5f and is thought to be better over this extra 1f distance. Still looks progressive. Worth an each-way bet in a race that looks an open contest to me.
Most consistent mare in this grade. Won over a similar trip at Chelmsford 2 runs back and the 3rd in that race has won since.

Fine Print didn’t get the clearest run last time at Dundalk but still wasn’t beaten far and has been holding her form well. She’s up in trip here and tries Tapeta for the first time, which could suit. On the balance of her form, she looks a bit of value and could run a big race if things fall right.

Two Plus Two is in decent nick, winning here in January and backing that up with a solid second last time. The trip might just push his stamina to the edge, but he’s clearly in form and should be thereabouts again if he sees it out.

Race 8 at Wolverhampton today is the Gamble Responsibly At BetUK Handicap (Class 6) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 2,815 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Courageous Gold from the David M Simcock yard, and will be ridden by Josephine Gordon. This son of Magna Grecia is a lightly raced gelding and fared better again last time out after two poor efforts. Given this weak field and improvement likely, he could be a lurker here, no doubt. One for the shortlist.

Providing she still has some talent left at the age of 9 then she should be able to win this off a mark of 54. She was only beaten a head over CD last year off a mark of 57. Jason Hart takes the ride again and he's been successful in the past.
